title: Adaptive client application-datagram batching work item
summary: Add a cheap connection-local pressure classifier and one-way client promotion from contiguous UDP-segmented application bursts to the ordinary datagram path.
planned_changes: Add a connection-local adaptive batch policy, gate contiguous client application-datagram construction at the existing flush boundary, wire the same policy through the built-in client endpoint so Windows UDP segmentation is enabled only while eligible and disabled after promotion, preserve every individual-send boundary, add policy and endpoint-focused tests, add a permanent policy-cost benchmark, and run matched local c1/c4/c8/c16/c32 transport evidence plus download or duplex controls before deciding whether to retain the slice.
verification_plan: Validate the new SpecTrace artifacts; prove sparse, transient, sustained, and irreversible policy transitions; prove unsupported and rebound socket fallbacks; run focused batching, packet destination, ownership, loss rebuild, cancellation, disposal, and HTTP/3 tests; run BenchmarkDotNet Dry and Short jobs; run interleaved exact one-MiB established transport upload samples at c1/c4/c8/c16/c32 and at least one download or duplex guardrail; run the complete Release suite only if the candidate is retained; skip ProtocolLab unless the local gate passes.
out_of_scope: Changing the accepted listener/server segmented-burst path
Adding post-authentication stream executors or parallel connection-state mutation
Adding a generic asynchronous sender queue or accounting packets before platform submission
Hardcoding benchmark scenario names, payload sizes, or c16
Changing congestion control, flow control, recovery, ACK behavior, packet protection, ordering, cancellation, disposal, or public API
completion_notes: Implemented a built-in-client-only adaptive batching policy. It counts distinct queued stream identifiers into a fixed twelve-entry stack buffer, tolerates one transient pressured turn, promotes one way after repeated pressure, disables Windows UDP segmentation after promotion, and preserves individual-send fallback boundaries. Final focused coverage passed 65/65 after review fixes. BenchmarkDotNet Short measured the bounded pressure scan at about 41-55 ns with zero allocation. Adjacent exact one-MiB upload evidence passed without failures and improved c1/c4/c16/c32 medians by 90.1/17.3/6.4/46.7 percent respectively. The retained unconditional-client negative remains binding; this completed item does not claim to solve the broader c16 scheduler bottleneck.
